    Dune Meadows: Unbalanced Crossed-Nested Profiles

    dune-unbalanced-hybrid.Rmd

    Phase 26 treats a restoration treatment as crossed with regions while sites remain nested within regions. Unlike the balanced EMS analysis, regions may contain different numbers of sites, a complete treatment-by-region profile may be absent, and replicated treatment-by-site cells may have unequal sizes. The layout below is an analysis demonstration, not historical metadata for the Dune survey.

    Construct unequal complete-site profiles

    Regions contain two, three, and two sites. Region 3 has no treatment C profile. Every profile that is observed still contains every site in its region. One C cell has an extra observation, making that profile’s replication topology unique and therefore fixed during conditional permutation.

    site_counts <- c(R1 = 2L, R2 = 3L, R3 = 2L)
cells <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(site_counts), function(region) {
  nsite <- site_counts[[region]]
  treatments <- if (region == "R3") c("A", "B") else c("A", "B", "C")
  cell <- expand.grid(
    treatment = treatments, site_number = seq_len(unname(nsite)),
    KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  cell$region <- region
  cell
}))
cells$replicates <- 1L
cells$replicates[
  cells$region == "R2" & cells$treatment == "C" & cells$site_number == 1L
] <- 2L

sampling <- cells[
  rep(seq_len(nrow(cells)), cells$replicates),
  c("treatment", "region", "site_number")
]
rownames(sampling) <- NULL
sampling$replicate <- ave(
  seq_len(nrow(sampling)),
  interaction(sampling$treatment, sampling$region, sampling$site_number),
  FUN = seq_along
)
sampling$treatment <- factor(sampling$treatment, levels = c("A", "B", "C"))
sampling$region <- factor(sampling$region, levels = c("R1", "R2", "R3"))
sampling$site <- factor(paste(sampling$region, sampling$site_number, sep = "_"))
sampling
#>    treatment region site_number replicate site
#> 1          A     R1           1         1 R1_1
#> 2          B     R1           1         1 R1_1
#> 3          C     R1           1         1 R1_1
#> 4          A     R1           2         1 R1_2
#> 5          B     R1           2         1 R1_2
#> 6          C     R1           2         1 R1_2
#> 7          A     R2           1         1 R2_1
#> 8          B     R2           1         1 R2_1
#> 9          C     R2           1         1 R2_1
#> 10         C     R2           1         2 R2_1
#> 11         A     R2           2         1 R2_2
#> 12         B     R2           2         1 R2_2
#> 13         C     R2           2         1 R2_2
#> 14         A     R2           3         1 R2_3
#> 15         B     R2           3         1 R2_3
#> 16         C     R2           3         1 R2_3
#> 17         A     R3           1         1 R3_1
#> 18         B     R3           1         1 R3_1
#> 19         A     R3           2         1 R3_2
#> 20         B     R3           2         1 R3_2

    The 20 constructed observations use all 20 Dune community rows. Bray–Curtis geometry is aggregated in two explicit stages: observations are averaged within treatment-by-site cells, then site-cell centroids receive equal weight within each treatment-by-region profile.

    design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment +
    (1 | region/site) +
    (1 | treatment:region) +
    (1 | treatment:region:site),
  sampling,
  vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
)

    Test treatment after region adjustment

    The profile model is additive region + treatment. Its denominator is the remaining profile-centroid residual, used descriptively; Phase 26 makes no parametric unbalanced EMS claim. Intact profiles permute only within region and identical ordered site-cell sizes.

    fit <- permanova_unbalanced_hybrid(
  design,
  permutations = "all",
  keep_permutations = TRUE
)
fit$table
#>                        term df        ss         ms pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1                 treatment  2 0.1112795 0.05563976   0.6074   0.75
#> 2 Profile-centroid Residual  3 0.2748095 0.09160317       NA     NA
fit$test[c(
  "estimand", "permutation_strata", "attainable_permutations",
  "exact_permutation", "warnings"
)]
#> $estimand
#> [1] "equally weighted complete-site treatment-by-region profile centroids with additive region adjustment"
#> 
#> $permutation_strata
#> [1] "region crossed with exact site-specific cell-count topology"
#> 
#> $attainable_permutations
#> [1] 24
#> 
#> $exact_permutation
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $warnings
#> [1] "Inference is empirical on profile centroids; no unbalanced parametric EMS or variance-component claim is made."
#> [2] "Empirical inference retained the complete non-Euclidean Gower spectrum."

    Use the same profile scale for contrasts

    Planned and pairwise contrasts share the equal-site-weight profile geometry, one common equal-weight region reference grid, and the identical topology restrictions. The max-F family claims weak control only under the complete treatment-null randomization hypothesis.

    planned <- rbind(
  `A - B` = c(A = 1, B = -1, C = 0),
  `AB - C` = c(A = 0.5, B = 0.5, C = -1)
)
planned_fit <- permanova_mixed_contrasts(
  design, planned, permutations = "all", adjust = "holm"
)
planned_fit$table
#>        contrast
#> A - B     A - B
#> AB - C   AB - C
#>                                                                                                    estimand
#> A - B  equally weighted complete-site treatment-by-region profile centroids with additive region adjustment
#> AB - C equally weighted complete-site treatment-by-region profile centroids with additive region adjustment
#>        df         ss                                              denominator
#> A - B   1 0.09795274 MS[profile-centroid Residual after region and treatment]
#> AB - C  1 0.01332678 MS[profile-centroid Residual after region and treatment]
#>        denominator_df  pseudo_f p_perm p_adjusted adjustment
#> A - B               3 1.0693161    0.5          1       holm
#> AB - C              3 0.1454838    1.0          1       holm

family_fit <- permanova_mixed_maxT_pairwise(
  design, permutations = "all"
)
family_fit$table

    Know the boundary

    A partially observed profile is not equivalent to a missing whole profile: its site composition would change the estimand and could import site effects into a treatment comparison. Phase 26 therefore rejects partial site profiles, disconnected treatment-by-region incidence, topology strata that cannot move every treatment contrast, and numerically zero profile residual denominators. Random slopes, multiple hierarchy trees, and unbalanced parametric variance components remain outside this empirical engine.
